title: Hanthawaddy Kingdom
capsule: Hanthawaddy (Pegu) was a Mon kingdom in lower Burma founded in 1287 after the Mongol-induced collapse of Pagan, reaching its cultural and political apex under King Razadarit (r. 1385–1423), who repelled repeated Avan invasions in the Forty Years' War and secured Mon independence. The reign of Shin Sawbu (r. 1453–1472) and her successor Dhammazedi (r. 1472–1492) saw the kingdom become a renowned Theravada Buddhist center; Dhammazedi's Kalyani Inscriptions of 1476 record a mission to Sri Lanka to purify the monastic ordination lineage. The Toungoo king Tabinshwehti conquered Pegu in 1539 and fully absorbed the kingdom by 1541, ending Mon autonomy; a brief Mon restoration in 1550–1552 collapsed when Bayinnaung recaptured Pegu in 1552.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The kingdom's core in the Irrawaddy delta and Pegu plains is documented in Burmese and Mon chronicles and Portuguese accounts; upland frontier zones are less precisely bounded.
